machine: Apple M5 Max, 128 GB, MLX 0.32.4, bfloat16
method: real en-zh shards (Translation Training Data/shards_v1), production 50M model_config, random init, same seed and data order per arm, 3-6 optimizer steps, valid CE on 6 fixed validation windows. long = attention_block_size 1024 + ce_chunk_size 1024 + moe_chunk_tokens 8192. Few steps: the CE column shows equal quality between arms, not final model quality.
conclusions: long vs base: 2.2x faster at 8k, 8.1x at 16k, with 5.4x and 10.2x less peak memory; base at 16k used 141.5 GB of the 128 GB machine.
valid CE differs by at most 3e-3 between arms: the options do not change what the model learns.

recompute_scope=mlp at 32k: saves 1.4 GB (5%) and loses 11% speed; whole-block recompute saves 6.9 GB (25%) and loses 19% speed. The memory saved per speed lost is better for whole-block, so mlp is only worth it when a little more memory is enough.
mla_upproj_recompute: no memory benefit (24.47 -> 24.29 GiB), 6.7% slower; ships off.
larger attention blocks help one MLA layer but hurt the full model (sliding-window layers); 1024 stays.
temporal_grad_span and lookahead_input_detach: neutral on this data (valid CE within 1e-3); ship off.
